sections.h2: How a West Virginia eviction starts
sections.html:
The landlord files a verified petition in the magistrate court or circuit court of the county where the rental sits. Section 55-3A-1 of the West Virginia Code lets an owner or the owner's agent ask for summary relief to remove a tenant from residential rental property.

The petition needs four things: a statement that the petitioner is the owner or agent with a right to recover possession, a short description of the property, the reason the tenant is wrongfully there, and a request for possession. The reason must be one of three: the tenant is behind on rent, has breached a warranty or leasehold covenant, or has deliberately or negligently damaged the property or knowingly let someone else do so. The petition describes the arrearage, breach or act.

The West Virginia Judiciary publishes a petition form titled Petition for Summary Relief, Wrongful Occupation of Residential Rental Property. It cites sections 55-3A-1, 50-5-8(a) and 37-15-3 and Magistrate Court Civil Rule 6A, and it must be sworn or affirmed before a notary.

The statute counts hearing and response periods in days, and it ties the no-cause route to the length of the tenancy.

Step or noticeTime periodAuthority
Hearing after petition is filedNot less than 5 and not more than 10 judicial days after filing55-3A-1(b)
Tenant's written defenseWithin 5 days of receiving the notice of hearing55-3A-1(c)
Answer under magistrate rulesWithin 5 days after service of the summons and complaintMagistrate Court Civil Rule 4
Jury demandWritten notice within 5 days of serviceJudiciary petition form
Year-to-year tenancy, termination noticeIn writing, at least three months before the end of any year37-6-5
Periodic tenancy under one year, no-cause noticeNotice for one full period before the end of a period37-6-5
Stored belongings after an orderLandlord may dispose after thirty days in listed cases55-3A-3(h)

Section 55-3A-1 sets no separate pre-filing notice period for the three grounds. A lease with its own notice terms can control, as covered below. If you're unsure which clock applies, call the magistrate court clerk or an attorney before filing.

A landlord can end a month-to-month or other short periodic tenancy by giving notice for one full period before the end of a period. Under section 37-6-5, a year-to-year tenancy ends with written notice from either side at least three months before the end of any year. A periodic tenancy shorter than a year ends by that same notice or by notice for one full period before the end of any period.

Service has rules. A notice meant for the tenant may be served on the tenant or on anyone holding under the tenant, and the same goes for any part of the leased premises. A tenant's notice to the landlord can be served on the owner or the owner's agent.

Two carve-outs apply. The section yields to a special agreement that fixes another notice period or says no notice is due. And no notice is needed for a tenant whose term ends at a certain time.

  • Year to year: written notice at least three months before year end.
  • Shorter periodic tenancy: notice for one full period.
  • Lease with its own terms: check the agreement first.
  • Fixed term ending on a set date: no notice needed under this section.

The court sets a hearing five to ten judicial days after the petition is filed, and the landlord must serve notice of it right away. Under section 55-3A-1(c), service follows Rule 4 of the West Virginia Rules of Civil Procedure or goes by certified mail, return receipt requested. The notice tells the tenant that a written defense must be filed and served within five days of receipt. The petitioner then files the petition with proof of service.

If the tenant doesn't appear, answer or respond by the hearing, section 55-3A-3(a) directs the court to enter an order granting immediate possession to the landlord. If the tenant answers, the hearing takes up the issues raised. On a rent claim, the tenant can argue the landlord breached a material covenant that the duty to pay rent depends on. On a breach or damage claim, the tenant can raise defenses to the petition. Section 55-3A-2 lets the tenant assert any defense available in an action for ejectment or unlawful detainer.

Continuances are for cause only, never as a matter of right. A tenant who gets one must pay into court any periodic rent that falls due while it lasts.

When the court finds wrongful occupation, it enters an order granting immediate possession and sets the date the tenant must leave. Under section 55-3A-3(f), the court weighs the nature of the property, such as furnished or unfurnished, the possible harm to each side, and other relevant facts in setting that time.

If the tenant stays past the date, the order directs the sheriff to remove the tenant forthwith, taking care to guard against damage to the property of both landlord and tenant. The sheriff does the removal, not the landlord.

On appeal, a winning tenant gets money damages only if the lease term has expired, unless there is an issue of title, retaliatory eviction or breach of warranty. During an appeal, a tenant has no right to stay if the tenancy has otherwise expired.

After a possession order, section 55-3A-3(h) gives the landlord three choices for items the tenant leaves. The landlord may dispose of them without liability if the tenant says in writing that they are abandoned or if they are garbage. The landlord may also remove and store them, or leave them on the property.

  • Stored items may be disposed of after thirty days if the tenant hasn't paid reasonable storage and removal costs or taken the property back, or if storage costs equal the value of the items.
  • Items left on the property may be disposed of after thirty days if the tenant hasn't paid the reasonable cost of leaving them or retrieved them.
  • Items worth more than $300 must be stored for up to thirty more days if the tenant or a secured party says they intend to remove them and pays the reasonable costs.

sections.h2: Selling a rental with a tenant in it
sections.html:
You can usually sell a rental while it is occupied, but a buyer who wants the house empty has to live with the timeline above. A petition, a hearing five to ten judicial days later, a possible defense, and then a court-set vacate date all come before the sheriff can act.

A conventional buyer who needs a vacant house, or whose lender won't close with an occupant, may walk away from a rental with a pending case. We buy houses as-is, so ask whether an occupied house is something we can take on. Read your lease, and ask a West Virginia attorney whether it binds a new owner.

  • Gather the lease, rent ledger and any written notices.
  • Note whether the tenancy is year to year, periodic or for a fixed term.
  • Photograph any damage before and after the tenant leaves.
  • Keep copies of what you served, and how.

The West Virginia Judiciary hosts the petition and a civil summons for wrongful occupation of residential rental property on its magistrate court forms page. The petition form carries a notice that any party seeking over $20.00 or possession of real estate may elect a jury trial, and that in wrongful occupation cases the election must be made in writing within 5 days of service or the right is lost.

faqs.q: How long must a West Virginia landlord wait before filing an eviction?
faqs.a: Section 55-3A-1 sets no separate waiting period for the three grounds: unpaid rent, breach of a warranty or leasehold covenant, and damage to the property. The hearing is set 5 to 10 judicial days after filing. Check your lease for notice terms of its own.

faqs.q: How long does a tenant have to respond to an eviction petition?
faqs.a: Five days. The notice of hearing tells the tenant a written defense may be filed within five days of receipt, and magistrate rules give a defendant 5 days after service of the summons and complaint to answer.

faqs.q: How much notice ends a month-to-month tenancy?
faqs.a: Notice for one full period before the end of a period. Under section 37-6-5, a periodic tenancy shorter than a year ends that way, and a year-to-year tenancy needs written notice at least three months before the end of any year. A special agreement in the lease can change this.

faqs.q: Can a landlord remove a tenant without a court order?
faqs.a: No. Under section 55-3A-3, the court's order sets the date to vacate, and if the tenant stays past it the sheriff removes the tenant. Removal is a court and sheriff process.

faqs.q: What happens to a tenant's belongings after an eviction order?
faqs.a: The landlord may dispose of items the tenant has declared abandoned in writing, or garbage. Otherwise the landlord may store the items or leave them in place, and may dispose of them after thirty days in the listed cases. Items worth more than $300 may need up to thirty more days of storage.
